hero.title: PO Shipping Address Guide
hero.lead: How the system decides *where every purchase order ships*, written for QA and Support. Start with the mental model, then use the interactive tool to confirm any case in seconds.
hero.pill: Intended behavior reference · Standard & Store orders

start.heading: How shipping works, in one minute
start.lead: Every order is broken into one or more **Purchase Orders (POs)**. Each PO is a document telling one party to send goods somewhere. The system answers a single question for each PO: **what address goes in the Ship To block?**
start.info: **The whole system is three inputs feeding one decision.** 1) **Which document** is this (Blank PO, Decorator PO, or Supplier Decorated PO)? 2) **Which flags** are set on the order or product? 3) The system walks a **decision tree** and picks one of seven possible **destination addresses**.
start.body: The goal is to route product through the right hands: a blank garment may need to reach a decorator before it reaches the customer; a finished item may go straight to the buyer; sometimes everything routes back to your own warehouse first.

docs.heading: The three PO documents
docs.lead: A single order can generate more than one of these. Each follows its own decision tree because they sit at different points in the production chain.

cards.title: Undecorated goods from a supplier
cards.body: Orders blank product from the blank supplier. If the item is decorated, the blank usually has to reach a decorator before going anywhere else.

cards.title: Sends work to a decorator
cards.body: Goes to the vendor doing the decoration when decoration is done by a *different* vendor than the blank supplier.

cards.title: Supplier also decorates
cards.body: Used when the product and its decoration come from the *same* supplier. Follows the same address logic as a Decorator PO.

docs.note: **Multi-decoration chains:** when an item carries decorations from several vendors, POs hand off in sequence, Supplier to Decorator 1 to Decorator 2 to final destination. Only the **final** PO ships to the customer (or Alternate address); every earlier PO ships to the _next_ decorator.

flags.heading: Settings & flags that drive the decision
flags.lead: These are the toggles a CSR sets on the order, product, or partner configuration. Each one can redirect where a PO ships.

table.effect: Opens the decorator routing branch (Blank PO).

table.meaning: A specific override address was entered on the order.
table.effect: **Highest priority.** Sends the final PO to that address.

table.flag: Ship to Us Instead of Decorator
table.meaning: Route blanks back to your own location rather than to the decorator.
table.effect: Triggers the Ship to Us branch on a decorated Blank PO.

table.meaning: Route goods back to your location instead of out to the customer.
table.effect: Triggers the Ship to Us branch on Decorator / Supplier Decorated POs, and on an undecorated Blank PO.

table.meaning: A warehouse is configured to receive Ship to Us goods.
table.effect: Ship-to-Us goods go to the Destination Warehouse Address, but only if the Prioritize Warehouse admin setting is also On.

table.meaning: The order is tied to a Corporate Identity location.
table.effect: Used as the Ship-to-Us address when no warehouse is set.

table.flag: Additional Decorations / This is the FINAL PO
table.meaning: Describe where this PO sits in the decoration chain. On their own they do not change the address.
table.effect: If another decorator comes next, this PO ships to the next decorator; if final, the normal checks decide.

priority.heading: Priority rules
priority.lead: When more than one flag is set, the system resolves conflicts in a fixed order. This single rule explains most "why did it ship there?" questions.

cards.title: Alternate Ship To
cards.body: If an Alternate address is set, it wins over Ship-to-Us and default routing on the final PO.

cards.title: Ship to Us settings
cards.body: If no Alternate address, Ship-to-Us routing (warehouse to corporate identity to partner) applies.

cards.title: Vendor / Order
cards.body: With no overrides, the Supplier PO ships from Vendor and the Decorator PO ships to the order shipping address.

priority.note: **Within Ship to Us there is a sub-priority:** Destination Warehouse, then Corporate Identity, then Partner Address. The Destination Warehouse step only applies when the admin setting "Prioritize Warehouse Address on Ship To Us Toggles" is On.

tool.heading: Address determination tool
tool.lead: Pick a document, flip the flags as they appear on the order, and the tool shows the exact destination, its data source, and the fields you should see in the address block.

flows.heading: Decision flowcharts
flows.lead: The same logic the tool uses, drawn out. Diamonds are flag checks; green boxes are destinations.

scenarios.heading: Scenario library
scenarios.lead: Worked examples of intended behavior. Search by keyword to confirm what should happen for a given flag combination.

rows.definition: A document instructing one party to supply/decorate/ship goods. One order can spawn several.
The last PO in a decoration chain, the one that ships to the customer or Alternate address.
Routing goods back to your own location (warehouse to corporate identity to partner) instead of onward.
A one-off override address entered on the order; highest routing priority.
